problems.title: Compare three district populations
problems.question: A city’s three districts total 45000 people. Three quarters of the first population equals half the second and three fifths of the third. Find the third population.
problems.idea: Use the reciprocals of the equal fractions.
steps: There are 15 ratio units, so one unit is 45000/15=3000.
The third district has 5 units.

problems.title: A number compared with 93% of itself
problems.question: A number is 14 greater than 93% of itself. Find it.
problems.idea: The difference is 7% of the number.

problems.title: Group four products
problems.question: Evaluate 15.5·20.8−3.5·9.2+15.5·9.2−3.5·20.8.
problems.idea: Group terms by the repeated decimal factors.

problems.title: Positive divisors of 648
problems.question: How many positive divisors does 648 have?
problems.idea: Use its prime powers.
steps: A divisor independently chooses one of four exponents of 2 and five exponents of 3.

problems.title: Adjacent supplementary angles with a percentage ratio
problems.question: One of two adjacent supplementary angles is 40% larger than the other. Find the larger angle.
problems.idea: Let the smaller angle be t.
steps: The larger angle is 1.4·75°.

problems.title: A perpendicular to a transversal
problems.question: Parallel lines a,b meet transversal c at A,B. One formed angle is 50° greater than another. K lies on a and KB⊥c. Find angle AKB.
problems.idea: First find the acute transversal angle.
formulas: u+v=180°, v−u=50°; a perpendicular turns the acute angle into its complement.
steps: The two transversal angles are 65° and 115°.
Triangle AKB is right at B. Its angle at A is the acute angle 65°.
The remaining angle at K is 180°−90°−65°.

problems.title: A nested fraction with mixed numbers
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac{(2.7-0.8)\cdot2\frac13}{(5.2-1.4):(3/70)}$.
problems.idea: Convert the mixed number and simplify the quotient.
steps: Cancel 1/3 and use 1.9/3.8=1/2. The result is (1/2)(7/70).

problems.title: Equal division ratios create a parallel segment
problems.question: C is on AB. M is on AC and N on BC, with AM:MC=BN:NC=3:2. AB=12. Find MN.
problems.idea: Measure the division points from C.
steps: The equal ratios imply MN∥AB and triangle CMN is similar to CAB.
Thus MN=(2/5)AB=24/5.

problems.title: Recover two numbers from fractional parts
problems.question: Two numbers sum to 45. One seventh of the first equals one eighth of the second. Find their product.
problems.idea: The equality fixes their ratio.
steps: The 15 ratio units total 45, so u=21,v=24.
Their product is 21·24.

problems.title: Subtract an intersection of number sets
problems.question: A is the set of two-digit positive integers, B the multiples of 3, and C the positive integers with remainder 2 modulo 4. Find |A\(B∩C)|.
problems.idea: Count the intersection inside the two-digit interval.
steps: Its two-digit members are 18,30,42,54,66,78,90: seven numbers.
Remove those seven from the 90 members of A.

problems.title: Follow a zigzag between parallel lines
problems.question: In the printed zigzag BCDEF between parallel AB and QF, the successive marked angles are 35°,48°,37°,6°. Find angle DEF.
problems.idea: Track each segment’s inclination to a parallel horizontal line.
formulas: An angle between two slopes on opposite sides of a parallel is the sum of their inclinations.
steps: CB rises 35° above the parallels. Therefore CD falls 48°−35°=13° below them.
At D, DE and DC make 37°, so ED rises 37°−13°=24° above the parallels.
EF falls 6° below the parallels. Thus angle DEF is 24°+6°.

problems.title: The last index with exactly 57 multiples of 11
problems.question: Among 1,2,…,n exactly 57 numbers are divisible by 11. Find the greatest n.
problems.idea: The 58th multiple must not yet be included.

problems.title: Count digit expressions under divisibility by 36
problems.question: The five-digit number 42a4b is divisible by 36. How many different values can a+4b have?
problems.idea: Divisibility by 36 means divisibility by 4 and 9.
formulas: The last two digits 4b force b∈{0,4,8}; the digit sum 10+a+b must be a multiple of 9.
steps: For b=0, a=8. For b=4, a=4. For b=8, a=0 or 9.
The corresponding a+4b values are 8,20,32,41. They are all different.

problems.title: Clock hands at 15:05
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between clock hands at 15:05.
problems.idea: The hour hand moves continuously.
steps: At 3:05 the minute hand is at 30°, the hour hand at 92.5°.
Their difference is 62.5°, less than 180°.

problems.title: Place a school using a round-trip distance total
problems.question: Villages A,B are 100 km apart, with 300 and 100 pupils. A school between them gives a total daily pupil round-trip distance of 30000 km. How far is it from A?
problems.idea: Count both directions for every pupil.
formulas: Let distance from A be d; total=2[300d+100(100−d)].

problems.title: Which count can be a number of segments?
problems.question: n points in a plane have no three collinear. Joining every pair produces k segments. Which listed k is possible:25,12,16,18,24,28?
problems.idea: Every unordered pair determines a different segment.
steps: The nearby possible counts are 10,15,21,28 for n=5,6,7,8.
Only 28 appears in the list.

problems.title: Smallest difference from a gcd and lcm
problems.question: Positive integers a≥b have gcd 6 and lcm 36. Find the minimum a−b.
problems.idea: Factor out the gcd.
steps: The coprime pairs with u≥v are (6,1),(3,2).
They give differences 30 and 6 respectively.

problems.title: Apply a piecewise operation twice
problems.question: Define a*b=a²−2b when a≥b and a*b=2b−a when a<b. Evaluate (1*3)*2.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate branch at each step.

problems.title: Supplementary angles and a right angle
problems.question: Angle KLT is five times adjacent angle TLN. K,L,N are collinear and angle TLF=90°. Find angle KLF as drawn.
problems.idea: The adjacent angles sum to 180°.
steps: Thus TLN=30° and KLT=150°.
The ray LF lies 90° from LT toward the side shown, so its angle with LN is 60°.
Because LK is opposite LN, angle KLF=180°−60°.

problems.title: Dilute salt water
problems.question: 40 kg of seawater contains 4% salt. How much fresh water makes the concentration 2.5%?
problems.idea: Salt mass remains unchanged.
steps: The final mass must be 64 kg.
Add 64−40=24 kg of water.

problems.title: Maximum regions formed by eleven lines
problems.question: What is the maximum number of plane regions produced by 11 lines?
problems.idea: Each new line meets every earlier one at distinct points.
steps: The kth line is split into k pieces and adds k regions, if no lines are parallel and no three concurrent.

problems.title: A percentage rises despite losing members
problems.question: Singers are 60% of an ensemble. After k members leave, the singer count drops by 7, but the singer percentage rises. Which listed k from 6,8,9,10,11,12 can work?
problems.idea: Write the percentage comparison with the reduced total.
steps: Multiplying by N−k>0 gives 0.6k>7, so k>35/3.
Only 12 is listed. It is possible, for example with N=25: singers drop from 15 to 8 and the ensemble from 25 to 13.

problems.title: Compare segments with outward rays
problems.question: Six points lie on a line. How many more segments than rays with endpoints at these points are there?
problems.idea: Count distinct segments and distinct rays on that line.
steps: Every starting point has one ray in each direction.
The difference is 15−12.

problems.title: A class size from two divisibility conditions
problems.question: A class has fewer than 30 pupils and three times as many boys as girls. Four pupils are absent, representing 20% of the class. How many are present?
problems.idea: Use the absent proportion directly.
steps: N=20, which is compatible with a 3:1 gender ratio.
The number present is 20−4.

problems.title: A number one short of several multiples
problems.question: Find the smallest positive integer leaving remainders 2,3,4,5 when divided by 3,4,5,6 respectively.
problems.idea: Adding 1 makes it divisible by all four divisors.
steps: Thus n+1 is a positive multiple of 60.
The smallest n is 60−1.
